_what: The ratchet ceiling for bed_pixels: how much of our own mattress the frame is allowed to show before the build fails. NOT the target - see best_on_record and target below.
_why_a_ratchet: A flat cut at the delivered value fails 15 of 15 masked frames in this lane history, because the bare flank is in every frame this studio has made. A rung red on every render gets switched off (R13). So the absolute number PRINTS on every run into the render path and what BLOCKS is the number rising - which is the half nothing caught when it rose 23x between p2r31e and p2r44 while coverage read 94.0% and fall_sides read 4/4.
_how_to_lower_it: A round that covers more of the mattress re-runs bed_pixels and writes the lower numbers here, naming the round. It may only ever go DOWN. Raising it is a decision that needs a row in qa/open-decisions.json saying why the bed is allowed to get worse.

best_on_record.note: the hand-built cloth stack covered the mattress 23x better than the bought set does. This is NOT an instruction to revert - his standing order is that the bed cloth is ACQUIRED (R13, class order, twice) - it is the proof that core near zero is reachable on this bed, this camera and this room, so the target is not a property of the frame.

target.note: three blind sighted readers over 7 delivered frames: 16 of 18 legible readings none, 2 sliver, 0 above sliver; ours most 3 for 3. The panel answers on a word scale and delivered frames carry no object mask, so no delivered flank can be counted in pixels - this target is a direction with a fact behind it, not a measured px value.
